incidents.victim: Oracle E-Business Suite users (payments processing)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a critical Oracle E-Business Suite payments flaw (CVE-2026-46817, CVSS 9.8), observed on honeypots before any public proof-of-concept existed.
incidents.impact: Researchers saw six exploitation attempts from a single IP in a two-hour window, likely reconnaissance and weaponization testing; roughly 950 vulnerable EBS instances remain exposed, more than half in the US, raising the risk of a broader campaign echoing last year's mass Oracle EBS extortion.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian critical infrastructure (electricity, water, government, military)
incidents.vector: Intrusions into regional utilities and state-owned entities deploying a novel 'TinyRCT' backdoor with anti-analysis features for reconnaissance and persistence.
incidents.impact: At least ten regional organizations compromised, including electricity and water providers and two state-owned entities, consistent with strategic pre-positioning rather than immediate disruption.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 users (finance, HR, logistics staff; public sector observed)
incidents.vector: A mature 'business email compromise-as-a-service' platform (ARToken, an affiliate of the EvilTokens phishing-as-a-service operation) abuses OAuth device-code flows to bypass MFA, then manipulates inbox rules and shared-access links to run fraud.
incidents.impact: AI-assisted, targeted invoice-themed lures that abuse real vendor relationships are used to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts; EvilTokens phishing volume reportedly rose roughly 1,380% year over year, giving attackers persistent access that survives password resets.

incidents.victim: Open-source software projects (Linux kernel, PHP, VLC, 7-Zip, OpenVPN, FFmpeg and others)
incidents.vector: A researcher used an AI model to fuzz code, then hand-built proof-of-concept exploits and published them publicly without notifying vendors ('Operation Exploratorium').
incidents.impact: More than a dozen zero-day exploits and write-ups across 15 widely used projects were dumped publicly (nine with assigned CVEs), giving attackers ready-made exploit code before patches exist; the researcher promised further releases.

incidents.victim: Aflac Japan
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to customer-facing and internal systems (initial access method undisclosed).
incidents.impact: Personal data of about 4.38 million policyholders exposed, including roughly 230,000 whose premium-payment account details were compromised; the insurer's second disclosed breach in about 13 months.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers (100+ orgs, mostly higher education; Nissan North America confirmed)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and extortion
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an actively abused Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (HR/CRM suite) to infiltrate networks and steal data for extortion.
incidents.impact: The extortion crew known publicly as ShinyHunters potentially infiltrated more than 100 organizations, predominantly universities, with Nissan North America among confirmed corporate victims; stolen data is being used to pressure victims for payment.

incidents.victim: Communications service provider (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager users)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a zero-day in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to escalate from a compromised administrator account to root-level access.
incidents.impact: Attackers obtained the highest level of access on SD-WAN management infrastructure at a communications provider, enabling full control of managed network devices.

incidents.victim: North American medical, academic, and military research institutions
incidents.vector: A sophisticated, targeted intrusion set that remained undetected for over a year across research organizations.
incidents.impact: Sustained espionage against North American research institutions, enabling long-term theft of medical, academic, and defense research.

incidents.victim: KDDI email systems (serving STNet, JCOM, Chubu Telecom, NIFTY, BIGLOBE)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in third-party software integrated with KDDI's email platform.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access to an email system supporting five Japanese ISPs; attackers may have obtained customer email addresses and passwords. The intrusion was detected and blocked.

incidents.victim: Nidec (Chaun Choung Technology, Taiwan subsidiary)
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on the Taiwan subsidiary's network; the BlackField group claims theft of over 2 terabytes of data.
incidents.impact: Subsidiary network encrypted with a $2 million ransom demand and alleged theft of employee, financial, procurement, manufacturing, legal, and IT records; Nidec's second ransomware incident in roughly 18 months.

incidents.victim: European and Asian hotels and accommodation providers
incidents.vector: Phishing emails impersonating guests with malicious LNK-laden zip files, abusing Calendly and Google redirects and PowerShell to drop persistent Node.js implants and a blockchain-C2 RAT.
incidents.impact: Multiple parallel campaigns since April 2026 established long-term access on hospitality networks for follow-on credential theft and lateral movement.

incidents.victim: US Department of Homeland Security (Homeland Security Information Network)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system between late May and early June.
incidents.impact: A DHS network used to share sensitive information with federal, state, local, and industry partners was compromised; the attackers and any exfiltrated data remain unidentified.

incidents.victim: Central Bank of Libya
incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion roughly three weeks earlier; the Qilin group stole and then leaked files on the dark web.
incidents.impact: Sensitive central-bank files were exfiltrated and published; Libyan authorities are investigating.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics
incidents.vector: Data-theft extortion by the World Leaks group, which exfiltrated and then leaked internal documents after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Around 200,000 documents were leaked, including iPhone prototype images and component designs from the Apple supplier.

incidents.victim: District of Columbia Housing Authority
incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting the agency's website and email server.
incidents.impact: Public-housing and voucher-services IT systems were disrupted, though the agency said scheduled payments would not be affected.

incidents.victim: SecondFi (cryptocurrency platform)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a bug in the platform's web wallet-generation software.
incidents.impact: About $2.4 million in customer crypto assets stolen; the platform entered maintenance mode and pledged to refund affected users.

incidents.victim: Government officials, military personnel, journalists, and activists (Ukraine, Europe, US)
incidents.attacker: Russia — FSB and military intelligence services
incidents.vector: Social engineering that masquerades as messaging-app support to steal Signal/WhatsApp backup recovery keys, verification codes, and PINs, and redirects Signal group invites to attacker-controlled devices.
incidents.impact: A long-running Russian intelligence campaign takes over encrypted-messaging accounts to read message histories and private chats; the US is offering up to $10 million for information on those responsible.

incidents.victim: Foxconn (North American factories)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack against the manufacturer's North American operations (details undisclosed).
incidents.impact: Foxconn confirmed a cyberattack disrupted North American factory operations.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiSandbox users
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a pair of critical FortiSandbox vulnerabilities that Fortinet disclosed in April, observed from multiple independent sources.
incidents.impact: Multiple security firms confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of the FortiSandbox flaws, warning the activity stems from several actors rather than a single campaign.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, healthcare systems, casinos, and retailers (47 US entities and others)
incidents.vector: SIM-swapping and SMS/voice social-engineering to steal credentials, followed by ransomware and extortion (the group known publicly as Scattered Spider).
incidents.impact: UK guilty pleas from two members tied to a spree of about 120 intrusions across 47 US entities and roughly $115 million in ransom payments, including attacks on Transport for London, SSM Health, Sutter Health, and major casinos and retailers.

incidents.victim: Klue and ~20 downstream customers (8x8, BeyondTrust, Deel, Jamf, Tanium, Snyk, Gong and others)
incidents.vector: Theft of OAuth tokens from Klue customer accounts, then abuse of Salesforce integrations to exfiltrate data from connected instances.
incidents.impact: A breach of the B2B sales-intelligence vendor cascaded into roughly 20 customer organizations via stolen Salesforce access, with the victim list still growing.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate / SSL VPN operators (global)
incidents.vector: Harvesting of exposed FortiGate configuration files and SSL-VPN authentication hashes, followed by offline GPU-cluster credential cracking and credential-stuffing against exposed VPN portals ('FortiBleed').
incidents.impact: Administrative and VPN credentials were recovered for tens of thousands of FortiGate systems across nearly 200 countries, with confirmed follow-on breaches reported (including a NATO defense contractor); offline cracking leaves victims with no login logs to detect the initial compromise. Allied agencies (UK NCSC, Australia's ACSC) issued warnings.

incidents.victim: Consumers via counterfeit Android TV boxes (1.4M+ IP addresses)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — proxy and ad fraud
incidents.vector: Pre-installed malware on unofficial Android TV boxes and pirated streaming apps enrolls devices into a botnet (linked to Vo1d) used as residential proxies.
incidents.impact: Millions of consumer devices were conscripted for advertising fraud, account takeovers, and mass data-scraping; a single May 2026 scraping incident spanned 1.4 million IP addresses.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (law-enforcement action)
incidents.vector: US prosecution of a Ukrainian national extradited from Ireland for a wire-fraud conspiracy tied to the Conti ransomware operation.
incidents.impact: Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to conspiracy connected to Conti ransomware, part of continued law-enforcement pressure on the group's operators.

incidents.victim: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft and extortion
incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft by the extortion crew known publicly as ShinyHunters.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended insurer risk designations and credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure; the attackers were evicted and operations are being restored.

incidents.victim: Fox Rothschild (law firm)
incidents.vector: Data-theft extortion by the Silent Ransom Group targeting the US law firm.
incidents.impact: The firm was breached and extorted in May; it declined to pay the ransom demand.

incidents.victim: Sapporo Holdings subsidiaries (Pokka Singapore, Sleeman Breweries Canada)
incidents.vector: Suspicious network activity detected on overseas subsidiaries, prompting systems to be taken offline.
incidents.impact: Two overseas subsidiaries were compromised and are under investigation for possible data theft; domestic Japanese operations were unaffected.
